rationale: Objective decomposition (measured): the frozen step issues exactly 13 cross-rank-matched NCCL allreduces through one dispatch target, c10d.allreduce_.default (op schema verified against the measured worker's torch 2.13.0+cu129): 12 buckets of 7,087,872 fp32 elements (group f833b57a373d8262a384, call d0938de87369efd500322679) plus the is-last embedding bucket of 39,385,344 elements (group 8525af72c631b94e3dd0, call b8ade439d7b8bd5fb5c1029b). inputs/project.json original_baseline: step_ms 141.17/141.31; objective (max-rank NCCL kernel sum) 62.14 ms on rank 0 (diag values 63.14/62.14/62.08) and 86.48 ms on rank 1 (values 86.48/83.72/86.99), so rank 1 carries ~21-24 ms above rank 0. Where the excess lives: inputs/observations/current/execution_timeline-1221e205.json cross_rank shows all 13 collectives matched on process group 0 with per-collective CPU submission spread bounds of ~14.9-16.0 ms, and the early rank's first NCCL kernel stretched to 18.5 ms vs its 3.6 ms pure duration (instrumented run comm sums: 78.80 ms early rank vs 64.01 ms late rank); the collector's own scope notes state this spread is CPU submission timing, not GPU arrival skew or transport duration, and kernel sums include device waiting (inputs/source/workloads.json communication_metric_caveat). Evidence-reading check on the synthetic calibration: inputs/observations/current/collective_calibration-1af5837f.json measured correctness-checked synthetic contiguous allreduces at the exact observed sizes/dtypes/ranks, with median completions 3.5768/3.6753 ms per 28.35 MB bucket and 19.4773/19.6584 ms for the 157.5 MB bucket (per-rank totals ~62.4/63.6 ms). Its own interpretation field states it is a synthetic reference at observed payload size/dtype, NOT a reproduction of model scheduling, NOT a lower bound, and its logical payload rate is not busbw or wire throughput; model critical-path savings must not be inferred from it. I use it only to size the wait component (observed kernel sums minus reference durations at identical payloads). Pure wire time, critical-path lower bounds, GPU-ready skew and residual post-rendezvous jitter were not measured and remain unknown. Change: replace both call IDs jointly (a joint scope is required because synchronizing only the 12 small buckets or only the large final bucket would leave the remaining dispatches staggered and the absorbed-wait pattern intact; the adapter, DDP bucket layout, payload bytes and NCCL transport are frozen invariants). On each eligible invocation the replacement first executes a CPU-blocking gloo barrier on the adapter's existing out-of-band control group (state['control'], the same group the source uses for pre-step barriers; a gloo group is created lazily and cached only if that group is absent) and then calls the parent c10d.allreduce_ unchanged through context.references with identical tensors, process group, ReduceOp.SUM, async_op and timeout, returning its (Tensor[], Work) result unmodified. Both ranks therefore submit each of the 13 collectives within sub-millisecond spread instead of ~15 ms; the wait that the early rank previously absorbed as in-kernel spin (counted by communication_kernel_sum_ms) moves to the CPU side of the barrier, which launches no NCCL or CUDA kernel and adds nothing to the objective, while remaining inside the measured step boundary. Expected effect to be tested: objective falls from 86.48 ms toward the reference-duration level, roughly 64-68 ms (-21% to -26%), with step_ms within the 1.05x constraint (~148.2/148.4 ms budget vs 141.2/141.3 ms baseline) because the migrated wait was already on the critical path and the added cost is 13 CPU-side gloo round-trips (selection estimates ~0.1-0.3 ms each) plus possible loss of compute/communication overlap on the early rank. Numerics, loss, gradients, parameters, bucket views and optimizer state are untouched: reduction operands, op and communicator are bit-identical, so collective_identity, logical_payload and the 13 cross_rank_collectives observations are expected unchanged; the gloo rendezvous carries no payload and mirrors the source's existing out-of-band control usage. No inputs/previous-feedback.txt and no inputs/previous-candidate/ exist; this is the first attempt. Route labels reported from inside the replacement: 'gloo-rendezvous+parent-nccl-allreduce' on the synchronized path, 'stride-skipped+parent-nccl-allreduce' when the stride parameter suppresses the barrier, 'unsupported-signature+parent-nccl-allreduce' on guard mismatch, 'rendezvous-unavailable+parent-nccl-allreduce' when no gloo group can be resolved (setup failure category), and 'rendezvous-failed+parent-nccl-allreduce' when the barrier raises at runtime (the parent collective is still issued so the peer is not stranded).

setup_work.build_time: build(context) performs no CUDA work, no weight or parameter transforms, no module.forward wrappers and no CUDA Graph capture. It binds the parent callables from context.references for both call IDs, resolves the rendezvous group from state['control'] (created by the frozen adapter in prepare as a gloo group) and reads the optional stride parameter. The mapping is returned for both call IDs on every rank, preserving collective participation.
setup_work.lazy_setup: Only if state['control'] is absent or not a gloo ProcessGroup does the first eligible call create one small gloo group via dist.new_group (collective, issued at the same eligible-call index on all ranks, CPU-only, cached under a lock). In this project the adapter always provides the control group, so no group is created inside measured runs; any lazy creation would be absorbed during the 2 warmup runs that precede the 5 measured repeats.
setup_work.synchronization: Per eligible allreduce dispatch: one CPU-blocking dist.barrier on the gloo control group (default async_op=False, group timeout 120 s, no device_ids, no CUDA stream interaction), then the parent NCCL allreduce is issued exactly as before. Barriers occur only at the 13 in-backward allreduce dispatches of the fourth micro-step; the no_sync micro-steps, optimizer.step and the completion-boundary synchronize are untouched. State lifecycle: reset(), zero_grad and the initial CPU state_dict snapshot are unaffected; nothing is cached across invocations except the resolved group object.
setup_work.memory: No CUDA allocations are added at setup or runtime, no graphs or retained graph pools are created, and the gloo rendezvous uses CPU sockets/store only. framework.peak_allocated_bytes, framework.lifecycle_peak_allocated_bytes and reserved pools are expected unchanged relative to baseline; no counter movement is claimed or required for this change.

quality_risks: Bilateral barrier obligation: the gloo barrier requires both ranks to invoke the replacement at the same eligible calls. The frozen workload issues identical 13-call DDP bucket schedules on both ranks and the eligibility guard depends only on the argument signature (single 1-D contiguous CUDA fp32 tensor of an observed numel), which is identical cross-rank by DDP construction, so guard decisions match; divergence would surface as a barrier timeout (~120 s) with the parent collective still issued afterwards rather than silent corruption.

cross_rank_collectives matching: the 13 NCCL allreduces are unchanged in op, operands, group and order, but per-call CPU-side gloo barriers are new in-window activity on the control group; the framework's runtime matching evidence must confirm they do not perturb the required cross_rank_collectives observation.

step_ms budget: the rendezvous throttles the early rank's autograd thread to the peer's pace, which can remove compute/communication overlap that previously hid inside stretched NCCL kernels, and adds ~13 gloo round-trips of CPU latency; headroom is ~7 ms against the 1.05x constraint. The rendezvous_stride=13 parameter variant (barrier only on the first dispatch of each 13-call sequence) reduces this overhead if per-call synchronization proves too costly, at the cost of leaving residual per-collective skew to be absorbed by the first post-rendezvous kernel.

Achievable floor is not guaranteed: residual CPU submission jitter after barrier release and GPU-side readiness differences between ranks are unmeasured; no claim is made that the synthetic reference-duration sum (~62.4-63.6 ms) is reachable, only that the observed ~21-24 ms in-kernel wait component is targeted.

If a barrier raises (for example on timeout), the replacement reports 'rendezvous-failed+parent-nccl-allreduce' and still issues the parent collective; a subsequent NCCL-side timeout would fail the run loudly instead of producing wrong numbers.

The gloo barrier count is exactly one per eligible dispatch (13 per run) on a group otherwise used only by the adapter's out-of-window pre-step barrier, so no concurrent use of the same process group occurs; this holds because the reducer issues bucket allreduces sequentially from one autograd thread.

params.name: rendezvous_stride
params.description: Run the gloo rendezvous on every eligible allreduce dispatch (1, primary hypothesis: maximum submission alignment) or on the first dispatch of each 13-call step sequence (13, one rendezvous per step: lowest CPU overhead, initial offset absorbed once). Collective semantics, payloads and results are identical for both values; only barrier frequency changes. Read from context['parameters'] with default 1.
